name: A person checking the decisions
summary: When your app makes a decision about someone, a person reviews it before it takes effect — and the reasoning is kept.

provenance.source: SimpleHire — its human-review requirement for AI screening decisions, where an automated recommendation never becomes an outcome on its own
provenance.changes: Generalised away from hiring into any consequential decision, and given an explicit state machine so 'a person reviewed it' is a recorded fact rather than an assumption.

extensionPoints.description: The screen your reviewers use. The rules about what counts as a review are not yours to change.

postInstall: Anything your app decides automatically should create a review item instead of acting.
Tell the people affected that a decision is being made about them, and that a person reviews it.
limitations: It makes the review happen and records it. It cannot make the review thoughtful.
No appeals process. If someone wants to contest a decision, you need one of those too.
It does not decide which of your decisions are consequential enough to need review. That is your judgement.
solves: a person checks the decision before it takes effect
approve or reject before it is final
someone signs off on automated decisions
